code.framework.web.why: Send HTTP requests to a service and receive correct, well-formed responses, including streamed events, upgraded WebSocket connections and error statuses.
code.framework.web.how: Accepts HTTP connections, routes each request to the application's handler and writes back the handler's response.

code.server.http.why: Accept network connections and turn each into HTTP requests for the application service.
code.server.http.how: axum::serve takes a listener and a make-service, runs hyper per connection and supports graceful shutdown.

code.router.http.why: Decide which handler or service receives each request so the application defines behavior per path and method.
code.router.http.how: Router matches the path with matchit, delegates to a MethodRouter, supports nest, merge, layer, state and fallbacks.

upstream.library.matchit.why: Match a request path against registered path patterns with named and wildcard parameters.
upstream.library.matchit.how: Holds a matchit Node and returns the matched route id and captured parameters.

code.service.route.why: Store every endpoint in one uniform callable form so any handler or service can serve a matched path.
code.service.route.how: Keeps a map of route id to Endpoint, where an Endpoint is a MethodRouter or a boxed Route.

code.router.method.why: Dispatch a matched path to the endpoint for the request method.
code.router.method.how: Calls the MethodRouter stored for the route id.

code.router.path.why: Resolve the request path to an endpoint, including nested routers and the fallback.
code.router.path.how: Router owns a PathRouter for routes and a second PathRouter for fallbacks and calls it for each request.

upstream.library.tower.why: Accept and apply tower layers and services so middleware and services compose with routes.
upstream.library.tower.how: Router implements tower Service for Request, and layer, route_layer and route_service take tower Layer and Service values.

code.listener.connection.why: Receive each new network connection with its peer address.
code.listener.connection.how: Listener::accept returns an IO stream and address; implemented for TcpListener, with ListenerExt adding tap_io and limit_connections.

upstream.library.hyper.why: Parse HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 on each connection and hand request bodies and responses between the socket and the service.
upstream.library.hyper.how: hyper_util auto Builder serves each connection and upgrades are enabled for WebSocket.

upstream.runtime.tokio.why: Perform asynchronous socket IO, spawn one task per connection and observe the shutdown signal.
upstream.runtime.tokio.how: tokio::spawn per connection, TcpListener for accept, and a watch channel for graceful shutdown.

code.router.http.why: Obtain the per-connection service that answers each request.
code.router.http.how: The make-service, usually Router::into_make_service, is called with IncomingStream and returns a cloned service.

code.handler.request.why: Run application logic for the matching HTTP method and obtain its response.
code.handler.request.how: The get, post, put, delete, patch, head, options, trace, connect and any functions wrap a Handler into a Route stored per method.

code.service.route.why: Hold each per-method endpoint, and the 405 fallback, as one uniform service.
code.service.route.how: Fields get, post and others are MethodEndpoint values, either Route or BoxedHandler.

upstream.library.http.why: Select the endpoint by request method and set the Allow header on 405 responses.
upstream.library.http.how: MethodFilter maps to http::Method; head requests fall back to get with the body removed.

upstream.library.tower.why: Erase the concrete type of any service or layered service so all routes share one type.
upstream.library.tower.how: Route wraps a tower BoxCloneSyncService, applies layers by boxing the result, and fixes the content-length of HEAD responses.

code.extractor.request.why: Build each handler argument from the incoming request before the handler runs.
code.extractor.request.how: For an async fn with up to 16 arguments, every argument but the last is FromRequestParts and the last is FromRequest; the first failure becomes the response.

code.response.http.why: Turn the handler's return value into a full HTTP response.
code.response.http.how: Calls IntoResponse::into_response on the output of the async fn.

code.listener.connection.why: Receive each new network connection with its peer address.
code.listener.connection.how: Listener::accept returns an IO stream and address; implemented for TcpListener, with ListenerExt adding tap_io.

upstream.library.axum_core.why: Define the contract that lets any type be built from a request.
upstream.library.axum_core.how: Re-exports FromRequest, FromRequestParts, FromRef, DefaultBodyLimit and Request from axum-core.

code.extractor.path.why: Offer the captured URL path parameters as typed values.
code.extractor.path.how: Path<T> deserializes route parameters stored in request extensions by the path router.

code.extractor.query.why: Offer the URL query string as a typed value.
code.extractor.query.how: Query<T> deserializes the query with serde_urlencoded.

code.extractor.state.how: State<T> clones T out of the router state, using FromRef to pick a part of it.

code.extractor.json.why: Offer a JSON request body as a typed value.
code.extractor.json.how: Json<T> requires a JSON content type, buffers the body and deserializes it with serde_json; it also serves as a response.

code.extractor.form.why: Offer a form-encoded body or query as a typed value.
code.extractor.form.how: Form<T> reads the query for GET and HEAD and the urlencoded body otherwise.

code.extractor.multipart.why: Offer multipart form-data uploads as a stream of fields.
code.extractor.multipart.how: Multipart reads the boundary from the content type and yields fields through multer.

code.extractor.websocket.why: Offer the HTTP upgrade to a WebSocket connection.
code.extractor.websocket.how: WebSocketUpgrade checks the upgrade headers; on_upgrade returns the 101 response and gives the handler a WebSocket after the upgrade.

code.extractor.connect_info.why: Offer details about the connection, such as the peer address.
code.extractor.connect_info.how: ConnectInfo<T> reads a value built from IncomingStream by into_make_service_with_connect_info.

upstream.library.serde.why: Deserialize query text into the caller's type and report which field failed.
Deserialize and serialize the JSON body.
upstream.library.serde.how: serde_json with serde_path_to_error; Json implements IntoResponse by serializing to bytes.

upstream.library.serde.why: Deserialize urlencoded text into the caller's type.

upstream.library.multer.how: multer::Multipart reads the request body stream and yields fields.

upstream.library.tungstenite.why: Frame, encode and decode WebSocket messages after the upgrade.
upstream.library.tungstenite.how: tokio-tungstenite WebSocketStream wraps the upgraded connection.

upstream.library.hyper.why: Take over the raw connection after the 101 response.

upstream.library.serde.why: Deserialize captured parameters into tuples, structs or maps.
upstream.library.serde.how: A custom serde Deserializer over percent-decoded parameter pairs.

upstream.library.serde.why: Deserialize query text into the caller's type and report which field failed.
Deserialize and serialize the JSON body.
upstream.library.serde.how: serde_json with serde_path_to_error; Json implements IntoResponse by serializing to bytes.

upstream.library.serde.why: Deserialize urlencoded text into the caller's type.

upstream.library.multer.how: multer::Multipart reads the request body stream and yields fields.

upstream.library.tungstenite.why: Frame, encode and decode WebSocket messages after the upgrade.
upstream.library.tungstenite.how: tokio-tungstenite WebSocketStream wraps the upgraded connection.

upstream.library.hyper.why: Take over the raw connection after the 101 response.

upstream.library.serde.why: Deserialize captured parameters into tuples, structs or maps.
upstream.library.serde.how: A custom serde Deserializer over percent-decoded parameter pairs.

code.server.http.why: Receive the per-connection value the server builds for each accepted connection.
code.server.http.how: The server passes IncomingStream, with remote_addr and the IO, to the make-service that stores the value in request extensions.

code.router.http.why: Receive the application state supplied to the router.
code.router.http.how: Router::with_state stores the state; each handler call passes a clone, and State reads it with FromRef.

upstream.library.axum_core.why: Define the contract that lets any type become a response.
upstream.library.axum_core.how: Re-exports IntoResponse, IntoResponseParts, Response and AppendHeaders; strings, status codes, tuples, Result and Json implement it.

upstream.library.http.how: http::Response with the axum Body; tuples set status and headers before the body.

code.response.sse.why: Offer a long-lived stream of server-sent events as a response.
code.response.sse.how: Sse wraps a Stream of Event values as a text/event-stream body, optionally with keep-alive comments.

code.response.redirect.why: Offer redirect responses without hand-building headers.
code.response.redirect.how: Redirect::to, temporary and permanent set the status and Location header.

upstream.runtime.tokio.why: Accept sockets and back off after accept errors.
upstream.runtime.tokio.how: Wraps tokio TcpListener and sleeps one second on non-connection errors.

code.router.method.why: Attach per-method handlers to a path.
code.router.method.how: route takes a MethodRouter and merges it when the path already exists.

code.handler.request.why: Serve unmatched requests and 405 responses with application logic.
code.handler.request.how: fallback and method_not_allowed_fallback accept a Handler.

code.middleware.function.why: Wrap all routes, or only matched routes, in cross-cutting behavior.
code.middleware.function.how: layer and route_layer accept the layers returned by from_fn, map_request, map_response and from_extractor.

upstream.library.tower.why: Plug into the layer system and call the rest of the stack.
upstream.library.tower.how: Each helper returns a tower Layer; from_fn gives the function a Next that runs the remaining stack.

code.extractor.request.why: Let middleware functions take extractors as arguments, and let from_extractor run an extractor as a gate.
code.extractor.request.how: from_fn, map_request and from_extractor run FromRequestParts extractors before the user function.

code.response.http.why: Turn the middleware's result into a response, or map the inner response.
code.response.http.how: map_response and from_fn convert return values through IntoResponse.

upstream.library.tower.why: Convert the fallible errors of any tower service into the Infallible error that axum routes require.
upstream.library.tower.how: HandleError and HandleErrorLayer wrap a Service and call an async function with the error.

code.extractor.request.why: Give the error function access to request parts.
code.extractor.request.how: The error function may take FromRequestParts extractors before the error argument.

code.response.http.why: Replace a service error with a response.

code.router.http.why: Check routing, nesting, merging, fallbacks and error handling behave as documented.
code.router.http.how: Builds routers, sends requests through TestClient and asserts on status and body; tests/panic_location.rs checks panic locations.

code.router.http.why: Measure request throughput for sample routers, such as minimal, basic, JSON and state routes.
code.router.http.how: Starts each router on a local port and drives it with rewrk.

upstream.tool.rewrk.why: Generate load and report latency and requests per second.
upstream.tool.rewrk.how: Runs the rewrk command and reads its output.

code.framework.web.why: Publish reusable tower layers and services that work unchanged inside axum applications.
code.framework.web.how: Accepts any tower Service or Layer wherever it takes a handler or middleware.

code.handler.error.why: Convert errors of a service route into responses so the route can be called with an Infallible error.
code.handler.error.how: MethodRouter::handle_error wraps the router in HandleError; ServiceExt::handle_error does the same for any service.

code.extractor.extension.why: Offer values that middleware or the server stored in request extensions.
code.extractor.extension.how: Extension<T> clones T from the request extensions; it is also a layer that inserts T and a response part that adds T to the response.

code.body.http.why: Read the request body, bounded by a size limit, when an extractor needs its bytes.
code.body.http.how: Request<Body> carries the body; body::to_bytes collects it up to a limit and DefaultBodyLimit sets the 2 MB default.

code.extractor.path.why: Offer the captured URL path parameters as typed values, plus raw path and query views.
code.extractor.path.how: Path<T> deserializes route parameters stored in request extensions by the path router; MatchedPath, NestedPath, OriginalUri, RawPathParams, RawQuery and RawForm expose the same request data without typing.

code.response.http.why: Turn the handler's return value into a full HTTP response.
code.response.http.how: Calls IntoResponse::into_response on the output of the async fn; Handler::with_state, into_service, layer and HandlerWithoutStateExt wrap a handler as a tower service.

code.body.http.why: Carry the response payload as a streamable body.
code.body.http.how: Response<Body> is the response type; strings, bytes and streams convert into Body.

upstream.library.matchit.why: Match a request path against registered path patterns with named and wildcard parameters.
upstream.library.matchit.how: An internal PathRouter holds a matchit Node, one for routes and one for fallbacks, and returns the matched route id and captured parameters.

code.service.route.why: Store every endpoint in one uniform callable form so any handler or service can serve a matched path.
code.service.route.how: The internal PathRouter keeps a map of route id to Endpoint, where an Endpoint is a MethodRouter or a boxed Route.

code.extractor.path.why: Offer the captured URL path parameters as typed values, plus raw path and query views.
code.extractor.path.how: Path<T> deserializes route parameters stored in request extensions by the router; MatchedPath, NestedPath, OriginalUri, RawPathParams, RawQuery and RawForm expose the same request data without typing.
